newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: FOREIGN BANKS URGED TO BE BACK IN MANILA FOREX MKT.
newsitem.headline: FOREIGN BANKS URGED TO BE BACK IN MANILA FOREX MKT.

text.p: Foreign banks which were kept out of the Philippine Dealing System (PDS) after the peso's effective devaluation should be allowed to trade on the system again, a Bankers Association of Philippines (BAP) official said.
Mike Aguilar, vice chairman of the BAP's open market committee told reporters on Thursday he would recommend to the BAP's board that foreign banks be allowed to trade on the PDS as soon as possible.
The PDS is the computerised trading system among banks on the peso/dollar.
Two weeks ago, the BAP asked foreign banks to stay away from the spot market to ease the pressure on the peso after its de facto devaluation on July 11.
"Since it's a normal market, I think we should allow them (the foreign banks) to come in. That's what the open market committee is recommending," Aguilar said.
The dollar is now being traded in the parallel market at only 10 to 15 centavos higher than the official market which was a sign the Philippine currency was normalising, he said.
Asked when the restriction on foreign banks could be lifted, Aguilar said: "We would wish as soon as possible. Hopefully as soon as Monday."
"Foreign banks are not only users of dollars but also providers," he said.
Aguilar also said the BAP decided to lift the "gentleman's agreement" not to let the peso go below 29 to the dollar.
The peso, along with other currencies in the region, was severely hit by speculation and the central bank spent nearly $2 billion in a futile defence since April.
The pressure remained even after the de facto devaluation but bankers said it seemed to have eased this week.
